title: No separate Massachusetts child-resistant packaging requirement for dispensed prescription drugs was found in the sources searched
subtopic: Child-resistant packaging of dispensed drugs: Massachusetts sources searched
rule_summary: As of 2026-09-16, no Massachusetts statute or regulation searched states a child-resistant or special packaging requirement of its own for prescription drugs dispensed by a pharmacy. M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 requires the pharmacist filling a prescription for a controlled substance to package it in a container and affix a label with the stated information, without a child-resistance element. A search of the General Laws on malegislature.gov for child-resistant, child resistant, special packaging, poison prevention, safety closure and safety cap returned child-resistant packaging provisions only for liquid nicotine and nicotine substances (M.G.L. c. 270, s. 27) and cannabis (M.G.L. c. 94G, s. 4), and nothing for dispensed drugs. The 12/6/2024 publication of 247 CMR 9.00, including the compliance packaging conditions in 247 CMR 9.08, and the current 105 CMR 700.000 contain no child-resistant or special packaging requirement. Under 15 U.S.C. 1476(a), while a federal special packaging standard is in effect for a household substance, a State may not establish or continue in effect a non-identical special packaging standard for it, except as 1476(b) and (c) provide.
exam_relevance: Tests that the child-resistant container rule for dispensed oral prescription drugs in Massachusetts is the federal Poison Prevention Packaging Act, and that Massachusetts compliance packaging rules neither replace it nor add a separate child-resistance standard.

authority.name: Packaging and labeling by pharmacist filling prescription

common_confusions: Assuming 247 CMR 9.08 sets its own child-resistance standard for compliance packages.
Assuming a State may relax the federal special packaging requirement for dispensed drugs.
verification_notes: On malegislature.gov the General Laws were searched for the phrases child-resistant, child resistant, special packaging, poison prevention, safety closure and safety cap, and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 was read. The official mass.gov PDFs of 247 CMR 9.00 (12/6/2024) and 105 CMR 700.000 were decoded with no stream decoding failures and searched for child, poison, safety closure and closure wording. Work done during the authoring session of 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-17.
